respuesta.pregunta: In which version of vendor-stockkeeper-api can I find the explanation of why checking for test items matters before touching the inventory flows? I mean the part about the risks you run if you skip that check.
respuesta.respuesta:
That explanation is in the important.md guide for version 0.0.10-stock-consumer, under the section on why verification matters [vendor-stockkeeper-api/0.0.10-stock-consumer/guide/important.md:L16-L21]. It gives three reasons:

- If test items are missing, you can end up with inventory errors [vendor-stockkeeper-api/0.0.10-stock-consumer/guide/important.md:L18-L18].
- The data sent to the item API has to be correct to keep the system's integrity intact [vendor-stockkeeper-api/0.0.10-stock-consumer/guide/important.md:L19-L19].
- A wrong movement can change the inventory status directly, which causes discrepancies and operational problems [vendor-stockkeeper-api/0.0.10-stock-consumer/guide/important.md:L20-L20].

I can only back this up for 0.0.10-stock-consumer. The documentation I retrieved doesn't let me confirm the same content for 0.0.3-paused-seller, 0.0.6-ep-restock-man or latest. That doesn't mean those versions lack it.
answer_checks: Identifies 0.0.10-stock-consumer as a version that documents the importance of verifying test items, citing its important.md (lines 16-21 or a subrange).
Mentions at least one of the documented reasons (inventory errors, item API/system integrity, unwanted alterations of inventory status causing discrepancies).
Does not claim that the section does not exist in 0.0.3-paused-seller, 0.0.6-ep-restock-man or latest.
Does not cite lines 16-21 of the important.md of 0.0.3-paused-seller, 0.0.6-ep-restock-man or latest as support.
Does not ask the user for a version.
